description: `retrieval.reindexPlan` (S54 T2, SP2) answers what a rebuild WOULD do and WOULD cost without doing any of it: the numbers come from the SAME estimate walk the query-side priced refusal already runs (files, stale files, chunks, ~tokens at bytes/4), and the cost rides the SAME three-state pricing the status drift uses — known carries the figure, unknown carries the sentence, never a bare number and never the $0.00 a configured-but-unpriced route would invite (O3/M30). It takes no embedder by its own signature: a preview that embedded to price itself charged for the preview. willReplaceEmbeddings is the corpus row's own history — a never-embedded corpus CREATES vectors, it replaces none. The corpus is NAMED (O8, no default) and an unknown one is refused (-31957), not estimated.

result.estimateBasis: approximately 4 bytes per token over the chunk bodies — the conventional English-text approximation, not a provider's tokenizer
